comparisonQuestion: Does foliage growing from branch-local sockets look more connected and natural than an assembled canopy, without becoming repetitive or popcorn-like?
runtimeRenderer: @storytree/app-surface SceneView through the real Studio SemanticGrowthDemo consumer

islandControl.status: held unchanged for comparison; owner evidence says it is still below LOOK bar because it reads as fading in
islandControl.implementation: The standard SemanticGrowthDemo frames() and app-owned SVG island path; no native-island override and no raster island.

hierarchy.clusterParentRule: Every cluster is rendered as a child of its owning branch group at an explicit branch-local socket.
hierarchy.painterRule: Clusters paint in recorded order beneath parent branch wood; trunk then paints over branch joins.
hierarchy.secondaryAction: One bounded 4.5% scale overshoot and small rotational settle per cluster; no loop.
hierarchy.stagger: Eight overlapping app-owned bloom windows from progress 0.58 through 0.865.

leafFamily.variation: Asymmetric sockets, mirror flags, rest rotations and scales vary the three assets across eight instances.

inheritedStrongestRound1Parts.ownerEvidence: Cutout-puppet trunk and plant growth were strongest; its detached canopy was rejected and is not reused.

authorImportBoundary.policy: Generated wood is retained only in raw provenance. Import keeps foliage and its outline, normalizes the crop to 64x64, and guarantees opaque socket coverage before runtime.
